model: Mass-weighted planet/satellite systems; fixed-element Kepler approximation where no satellite ephemeris is available

sources.name: Astronomy Engine v2.1.19
sources.usage: Earth and GeoMoonState are geocentric/heliocentric body-center states; JupiterMoons gives jovicentric states. Preserve supplied planet body centers. Treat the integrated Pluto system solution as the system barycenter.

sources.name: IAU WGCCRE 2015 (Archinal et al. 2018)
sources.usage: Pluto/Charon J2000 pole RA=132.993 deg, Dec=-6.163 deg, Pluto W0=302.695 deg. Near-circular synchronous approximation for Charon, not a precision satellite ephemeris.

sources.name: Stellarium solar system catalog
sources.usage: Cross-check separation 19596 km, radii Pluto 1188.3 km and Charon 606 km; physical/orbital constants only.

sources.name: JPL Solar System Dynamics satellite physical parameters
sources.usage: Approximate individual satellite mass ratios; existing catalog elements for other satellites retained.

limitations: Only direct planet/satellite systems are supported; rings are not mass-bearing satellites.
The Sun remains the heliocentric display origin; this is not an N-body integration of the whole Solar System.
For multiple moons, local orbit lines are instantaneous osculating paths with other moons held at their current offsets.
Charon uses a fixed circular approximation with 6.3872273-day period, in both precision modes. Long-term phase is illustrative.
Visibility switches affect drawing only, never the mass budget.

catalogEditing.storage: Built-in overrides and custom objects are stored separately in this browser. Built-in entries can be restored without deleting custom satellites.
catalogEditing.units: Mass is individual body mass / solar mass; radius is Earth radii; satellite semi-major axis is parent-relative separation in AU. Angles use J2000 ecliptic degrees; optional epochJD is Julian date, periodDays is days.
catalogEditing.missingMass: Unknown masses are never inferred. A missing parent mass requires an explicit satellite period and disables barycentric reaction. Missing satellite mass gives a massless tracer and a visible diagnostic.
catalogEditing.precisionPolicy: Unchanged systems retain supported precision ephemerides. Altered masses/orbits or new satellite membership cause that system to use the supplied Kepler parameters; cosmetic edits retain precision ephemerides.
catalogEditing.referenceDefault: A root newly acquiring satellites defaults to system-barycenter when no orbitReference was specified. Explicit body references remain supported.
catalogEditing.periodPriority: An explicit periodDays overrides the mass-derived two-body period; satellite discrepancies larger than 2% produce a diagnostic without changing the input. Mass still controls barycenter allocation.
